page.running_head: MADE BY A JESUIT IN IRELAND.

main_text.p: lated this canon out of that council into his collectionAddit. 3. cap. 31. edit. Pithæi. et Lindenbrogii.: which Bellarmine, as it seemeth, having some way heard of, knew not to distinguish between those capitularia, and Theodore's penitential; being herein as negligent as in his allegation of the fourth book of the sentences; where the master doth not bring in this sentence at all, but, having among other questions propounded this also for one, "WhetherUtrum sufficiat peccata confiteri soli Deo, an oporteat confiteri sacerdoti. Quibusdam visum est sufficere, si soli Deo fiat confessio, sine judicio sacerdotali et confessione Ecclesiæ. quia David dixit; Dixi, confitebor Domino, &c. non ait, sacerdoti: et tamen remissum sibi peccatum dicit. Petr. Lombard. lib. 4. sentent. dist. 17. it be sufficient that a man confess his sins to God alone, or whether he must confess to a priest," doth thereupon set down the diversity of men's opinions touching that matter; and saith, that "unto some it seemed to suffice, if confession were made to God only without the judgment of the priest, or the confession of the Church; because David said, I said, I will confess unto the Lord: he saith not, unto the priest; and yet he sheweth that his sin was forgiven him." For in these points, as the same author had before noted, "EvenIn his enim etiam docti diversa sentire inveniuntur: quia super his varia ac pene adversa tradidisse videntur doctores. Ibid. the learned were found to hold diversly: because the doctors seemed to deliver divers and almost contrary judgments therein."

The diverse sentences of the doctors touching this question, whether external confession were necessary or not, are at large laid down by Gratian: who in the end leaveth the matter in suspense, and concludeth in this manner: "UponQuibus auctoritatibus, vel quibus rationum firmamentis, utraque sententia innitatur, in medium breviter exposuimus. Cui autem harum potius adhærendum sit, lectoris judicio reservatur. Utraque enim fautores habet sapientes et religiosos viros. De pœnit. dist. 1. cap. 89. Quamvis. what authorities, or upon what strength of reasons both these opinions are grounded, I have briefly laid open. But to whether of them we should rather cleave, is reserved to the judgment of the reader. For both of them have for their favourers both wise and religious men." And so the matter rested undetermined
